newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian court delays ruling in Abiola case.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian court delays ruling in Abiola case.

text.p: A Nigerian court on Wednesday delayed ruling on the release of three veteran opposition figures held in an investigation into the murder of the wife of detained presidential contender Moshood Abiola.
"A ruling has not yet been prepared," judge Abdul Kafarati told the Lagos court by telephone. The case was adjourned until October 11.

Three leading figures in the opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) -- Abraham Adesanya, Ayo Adebanjo and Ganiyu Dawodu -- have been detained since June to help the police inquiry into the murder of Kudirat Abiola. They have not been charged.
Abiola's wife was shot in the head while driving along a Lagos street on June 4.
In July a court ruled the detention of the three men unlawful. But the police appealed against the ruling.
Abiola's vocal wife led the campaign to free him and install him as president in line with the results of a 1993 election, annulled by a former military government.
NADECO has also been campaigning for the military rulers to release Abiola, detained since 1994 when he declared himself president.
The hunt for the killers has yet to produce results. Last week the detective heading the investigation, Archibong Nkana, was retired.
